---
title: "ULMS RDP Setup"
subtitle: "Ubuntu / WSL2 → ULMS Windows Server, in about 10 minutes"
---

## What this guide gives you

A single command — `rdp-work` — that opens a full-screen, HiDPI-aware remote
desktop session on the ULMS Windows server, with your clipboard shared and a
local folder mounted inside Windows for drag-and-drop file transfer. No password
typed, no plain-text secrets in your dotfiles.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
This is a community write-up by and for ULMS users. It is not an official
University IT document. Always follow your institution's IT and information
security policies — in particular, never publish the server address, your
credentials, or research data to a public repository.
:::

## The four moving parts

| Component | What it does |
|---|---|
| **FreeRDP** (`xfreerdp`) | The RDP client. Handles dynamic resolution, clipboard, and drive redirection. |
| **GNOME Keyring** (`secret-tool`) | Encrypts your Windows password at rest so it never appears in `~/.bashrc` or your shell history. |
| **`~/rdp_share`** | A local folder that appears inside Windows as `\\tsclient\share`. |
| **`rdp-work`** | A one-word wrapper that wires the three together. |

## How the pieces fit together

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A["<b>rdp-work</b><br/>alias or script"] --> B["<b>secret-tool lookup</b><br/>reads encrypted password"]
    B --> C[("GNOME Keyring<br/>encrypted store")]
    A --> D["<b>xfreerdp</b><br/>RDP client"]
    C -.password.-> D
    D <==>|"RDP over VPN"| E["<b>ULMS Windows Server</b>"]
    F[("~/rdp_share<br/>local folder")] <-->|drive redirection| D
    E -.mounted as.- G["\\tsclient\share"]
```

## Read this in order

1. [**Core Setup**](setup.qmd) — the five steps everybody needs. Do these first, in order.
2. [**Tips & Hacks**](hacks.qmd) — optional quality-of-life shortcuts, including how to
   stop the keyring prompting you on every launch. These trade some security for

3. [**Troubleshooting**](troubleshooting.qmd) — what to do when the handshake fails,

::: {.callout-important}
## Before you start

You need an active **VPN connection** to the university network if you are off
campus, and a Windows account that is authorised for Remote Desktop on the
target server. Neither of those is covered here — ask ULMS IT if you are unsure.
:::

## Conventions used in this guide

Throughout, `<ULMS_SERVER_IP>` stands for the ULMS Windows server address and
`<WINDOWS_USER>` for your Windows account name. Rather than editing those into
every command by hand, the [Core Setup](setup.qmd) puts them in a single
`config.env` file that the launcher reads.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
Every code block on this site has a copy button in its top-right corner.
:::
